correctness.rationale:
At a source-defined Coulomb minimum, the exact equations are \(b=(1-\eta/a)/(1+y)\) and \(ya^2-\eta(2y+1)a+(1+y)(y^2-
u^2)=0\). The substitution \(\varepsilon=1/a\), \(y=\varepsilon Y\) creates a regular implicit-function problem with \(Y(0)=\eta\) and nonzero derivative. Its expansion gives \(y=\eta/a+(2\eta^2+
u^2)/a^2+O(a^{-3})\), and hence \(1-b=2\eta/a+
u^2/a^2+O(a^{-3})\). The independently inspected Coulomb zero expansion gives \(a_n=\pi n+\eta\log n+O(1)\), which yields the two claimed index limits.

value.rationale: The successive Coulomb minima are a new sharp-constant sequence in the fresh source. Quantifying their convergence is directly motivated by the theorem itself. The accepted result reveals a structural singular perturbation: fixed positive Coulomb charge changes the convergence order from the Bessel inverse-square scale to inverse-linear, with an explicit leading coefficient and logarithmic nodal correction. This describes the long-range Coulomb effect on the sharp inequality rather than merely refining a decimal constant.
